narratives.Overview:
## Summary

scope:complete replays acceptance before bank lookup and rejects swarm-only banks

## Context

Directive v0.109.1 in consumer bxc-3ci/FreshserviceAI. Issue #372 merged in PR #376 at 2890691ce96ea5e3e650cc6806b6e5c7f194b917 with all declared verification commands green. A fresh verify:ac bank at that exact HEAD recorded productStateHash fc7db5294dcf7a51b8a3656707fd115a46b443a5bbbeddc58e1d0a502420c48c. The active xBRIEF has plan.acceptance.commands=[] and six executable plan.metadata.swarm.verify_commands, including verify:scope-provenance and task check.

## Expected behavior

scope:complete should resolve and safety-check one acceptance command contract, reuse a matching green bank without executing those commands again, and execute every resolved command exactly once when no valid bank exists. A bank created from executable swarm.verify_commands should remain eligible when plan.acceptance.commands is empty. Changed commands, narrative captures, product state, or stale evidence must still fail closed.

## Actual behavior / gap

scope:complete invokes the standalone literal acceptance evaluator before its bank-aware completion walk. That evaluator rereads swarm.verify_commands and executes all six wrappers, so a fresh matching bank cannot suppress duplicate local work. Only afterward does the bank-aware path run, and its reuse check returns no bank when plan.acceptance.commands.length===0 even though verify:ac created the bank from the executable swarm ledger. In the consumer closeout, the pre-bank replay reached provenance and failed before any lifecycle mutation.

## Session notes

## Minimal reproduction

Use an active, approved xBRIEF with valid completion evidence and delivery evidence, plus:

```json
{
  "plan": {
    "acceptance": {
      "commands": [],
      "none_stated": true,
      "source_rung": "derived"
    },
    "metadata": {
      "swarm": {
        "verify_commands": ["<instrumented always-green command>"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

1. Run `deft verify:ac` at the merged product HEAD and confirm it records a green durable bank.
2. Reset the instrumented command's invocation counter.
3. Call `runTransition("complete")` or the equivalent `deft scope:complete` command with valid PR and merge evidence.
4. A matching bank should produce zero new invocations. The current transition invokes the command before it reaches the bank-aware walk.
5. Because `plan.acceptance.commands=[]`, the later reuse path also refuses the bank created from `swarm.verify_commands`; if the earlier execution remains green, the same ledger can be selected again by the later walk.

The FreshserviceAI #372 reproduction used six real wrappers and a fresh bank at merge commit `2890691ce96ea5e3e650cc6806b6e5c7f194b917`. Completion replayed the wrappers until `verify:scope-provenance` failed on the separate canonical-evidence defect. This is why a lifecycle-only closeout attempted local product validation again after the product and required CI were already green.

## Root cause evidence in v0.109.1

- [`scope/transition.ts:280-329`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.109.1/packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts#L280-L329) establishes the production order: per-item evidence gate, standalone `evaluateLiteralAcceptanceFromPlan`, then `evaluateScopeCompleteAcceptanceWalk`.
- [`literal-acceptance/evaluate.ts:249-260`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.109.1/packages/core/src/literal-acceptance/evaluate.ts#L249-L260) directly invokes the command runner and exposes no bank/cache option.
- [`literal-acceptance/capture.ts:580-639`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.109.1/packages/core/src/literal-acceptance/capture.ts#L580-L639) reads `plan.metadata.swarm.verify_commands` into that executable ledger.
- [`scope/acceptance-evidence.ts:515-556`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.109.1/packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts#L515-L556) reaches the product-first, bank-aware evaluator only after the standalone execution.
- [`product-first-done-gate/evaluate.ts:166-232`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.109.1/packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/evaluate.ts#L166-L232) contains the later bank-reuse check, including the refusal when `plan.acceptance.commands.length===0`.
- [`product-first-done-gate/acceptance-resolver.ts:274-277`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.109.1/packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/acceptance-resolver.ts#L274-L277) selects bank-only reuse for completion's later walk.
- [`product-first-done-gate/bank-aware-complete.test.ts:1-96`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.109.1/packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/bank-aware-complete.test.ts#L1-L96) tests `evaluateScopeCompleteAcceptanceWalk` directly, not full `runTransition("complete")`, so it cannot detect the earlier standalone invocation.

## Relationship to #3993

This partially overlaps [#3993](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3993). That issue observes the same literal-before-walk sequence, then focuses on a bank-served result losing the green-run fact (`runs: []`) and failing clause composition. This report covers two additional defects in the same transition:

1. a matching bank cannot suppress the standalone execution that occurs before lookup; and
2. the later reuse check refuses a bank created from `swarm.verify_commands` when `plan.acceptance.commands` is empty.

The fix should coordinate with #3993 so a consolidated bank-served result also retains the trusted green-run fact required by clause walking. That is a dependency/non-regression requirement, not a duplicate claim.

## Proposed fix

Consolidate completion onto one bank-aware acceptance path.

1. Resolve and safety-check literal, swarm, and narrative commands without executing them.
2. Include the resolved acceptance contract in bank eligibility, or store an equivalent trusted digest/fact.
3. If product state and the resolved contract match a valid green bank, serve completion from the bank with zero command replays.
4. Otherwise execute each resolved command exactly once.
5. Allow a bank minted from executable `swarm.verify_commands` to serve completion when `plan.acceptance.commands=[]`.
6. Preserve narrative-rescan, stale-product-state, changed-command, and failed-clause fail-closed guarantees.
7. Preserve the trusted green-run fact needed by clause-walk composition, consistent with #3993.

Simply deleting the earlier literal call is insufficient if bank eligibility does not bind the resolved command/narrative contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A real `runTransition("complete")` regression uses commands only in `swarm.verify_commands`, `plan.acceptance.commands=[]`, valid item evidence, and valid delivery evidence.
- [ ] With a matching green bank, the regression records zero new command invocations and completes successfully.
- [ ] Without a bank, every resolved command runs exactly once, never twice.
- [ ] A bank created from executable `swarm.verify_commands` is eligible even when `plan.acceptance.commands=[]`.
- [ ] A changed command ledger or newly captured narrative command invalidates or refuses reuse and causes at most one execution.
- [ ] A stale product-state hash remains fail-closed.
- [ ] Bank-served results retain the green-run fact needed by clause-walk composition as a #3993 non-regression.
- [ ] Tests cover both the direct acceptance-walk evaluator and full production transition ordering.
- [ ] A lifecycle-only completion with a valid matching bank does not invoke the consumer's generic local product build/test wrapper.
- [ ] No production skip flag, command deletion, or gate weakening is introduced.

## Workarounds evaluated

- Deleting or subsetting `swarm.verify_commands`, replacing them with no-ops, or changing the gate definition would violate gate integrity.
- Pre-marking items complete, manually moving the brief, or using internal test-only skips would bypass lifecycle gates.
- A valid human approval-only remint can address the separate provenance conflict, but completion still replays every declared wrapper, including `task check`; it does not make bank reuse work.
- There is no supported no-replay path in v0.109.1 for this shape.

Consumer reproduction: [bxc-3ci/FreshserviceAI#372](https://github.com/bxc-3ci/FreshserviceAI/issues/372), delivered by [PR #376](https://github.com/bxc-3ci/FreshserviceAI/pull/376). Consumer follow-up [#375](https://github.com/bxc-3ci/FreshserviceAI/issues/375) separately records the product requirement that canonical lifecycle-only local changes must not invoke `task ci:check`, `task check`, .NET setup, product build, or product tests.

## Verdict

The recorded refutation-target is not the whole remedy. One bank-aware complete path is the right chokepoint, and both cited defects are real at this SHA: the pre-walk executor always runs, and later bank reuse refuses empty `plan.acceptance.commands`. Matching and bank-serve reconstruction are still `plan.acceptance.commands`-shaped and omit `swarm.verify_commands`. A consolidation that only drops the pre-walk call and the empty-length guard would reuse a swarm-minted bank without binding or serving the swarm ledger.

Filing anchors re-checked at f96963e9 (origin/master). v0.109.1 line cites drift on `transition.ts` (now 297-343, not 280-329); order still holds. Other cited ranges still hold.

## 1. Bank eligibility and serve reconstruction omit the swarm ledger (`blocks-the-design`)

Evidence. `tryReuseVerifyAc` (`packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/evaluate.ts:209-231`) returns null when `acceptance.commands.length === 0`, then on a hit maps `commands` from `plan.acceptance.commands` and sets `runs: []`. `hashProductState` digests `{ acceptance: plan.acceptance, head, files }` and does not read `plan.metadata.swarm.verify_commands`. `AcPassBankRecord` stores product-state hash, scope id, head, and budget fields; it does not store commands or runs. Capture still loads swarm commands into the executable ledger (`literal-acceptance/capture.ts:625-639`). The pre-walk executor runs that ledger with no bank option (`literal-acceptance/evaluate.ts:24-34, 249-260`).

Failure mode. The filing shape is swarm-only complete: `plan.acceptance.commands=[]` plus executable `swarm.verify_commands`. Deleting `transition.ts:311-329` and `if (commandCount === 0) return null` would serve a matching product-hash bank as `commands: []`, `runs: []`, `resolvedCommandCount: 0`. Changing or adding `swarm.verify_commands` after mint would still match. Clause-walk would see no green-run fact (`evaluate.ts:728-729`). The filing already said deleting the earlier literal call is insufficient if eligibility does not bind the resolved contract. The recorded target compresses that bind into "including a bank minted from".

Disposition consequence. This lean cannot bind until eligibility matching and bank-serve reconstruction use the resolved literal+swarm+narrative contract from existing `resolveLiteralAcceptanceDetailed` (no execute), persisted at mint. `plan.acceptance.commands.length` is not that contract.

## 2. Reuse currently precedes resolve (`sharpens-framing`)

Evidence. `evaluateVerifyAcFromPlan` calls `tryReuseVerifyAc` at line 343, then `evaluateLiteralAcceptanceFromPlan` at 353. The complete profile is `reuseMode: "bank"` and `captureFromNarratives: true` (`acceptance-resolver.ts:274-277`).

Failure mode. If consolidation keeps try-reuse first, "resolve without executing" does not run before matching. Newly captured narrative commands and the safety-rejected ledger cannot invalidate a bank.

Disposition consequence. The single path must resolve and safety-check with no execute, then match, then execute each resolved command once on miss. That is a reorder of the existing walk, not a new evaluator.

## 3. Empty `plan.acceptance.commands` is three cases (`sharpens-framing`)

Evidence. Bank-aware tests still refuse empty stamped acceptance (`bank-aware-complete.test.ts`, soft_empty / #3334). `maybeBankOnAcPass` can bank a verified-pass with zero shell runs (`verifiedPass: true`). Swarm-only is a third case: empty `plan.acceptance.commands`, non-empty resolved executable ledger.

Failure mode. Treating `commands.length===0` as the swarm-only allow-list would also serve 0-run verified-pass banks and could skip the soft_empty refuse.

Disposition consequence. Swarm-only is eligible only when the resolved executable ledger is non-empty and equals the mint-time ledger. Truly empty stays refused.

## 4. Green-run fact already lives on the cache snapshot complete is profiled to ignore (`sharpens-framing`)

Evidence. `CachedVerifyAcSnapshot` stores `commands` and `runs` (`verify-ac-session-cache.ts:19-31`). Cache reuse copies those fields (`evaluate.ts:186-206`). Bank reuse does not (`evaluate.ts:225`). Complete uses `reuseMode: "bank"`, so it never reads the snapshot that has the fact. `clauseWalkBlocks` still keys `hasGreenExecutableRun` off `result.runs` (`acceptance-resolver.ts:236-244`). #3993 is that erasure on the finalize path.

Failure mode. Keeping the fact as a later #3993 hope, or treating any matching bank as a green run, either leaves swarm-only complete with `runs: []` or weakens the clause predicate without recording which commands ran.

Disposition consequence. #4060 owns persisting a cache-shaped mint snapshot onto the durable bank. Do not weaken `clauseWalkBlocks` to "servedFrom=bank implies green run". #3993 is a non-regression on this change, not a duplicate and not a deferral.

## 5. Production-order tests (`footnote`)

`bank-aware-complete.test.ts` calls `evaluateScopeCompleteAcceptanceWalk` directly, never `runTransition("complete")`. `runTransition` complete tests exist, but `skipAcceptanceEvidenceGate` is used at `transition.test.ts:512`, and none count invocations on a swarm-only bank. `restampCompletedBrief` does not run the acceptance walk; it is outside the consumer closeout path.

## Injection / swarm lens

This target changes what a swarm is allowed to re-execute after merge. `scope:complete` is the Phase 6 / complete-cohort chokepoint. Banks are unsigned files under `.deft/cache/ac-pass-banks`. Today `commandCount === 0` forces re-execution of swarm wrappers even when a product-hash bank exists. Removing that lock without putting the resolved swarm ledger into the digest lets a worktree-local bank at matching product hash authorize skipping whatever `verify_commands` now say, including a newly added `task check` / product build. The consumer filing wants that skip for a matching contract, not for a different one. Control: eligibility digest includes the resolved command contract; a `.deft/cache` write is not itself a green run of the current wrappers.

## Existing mechanisms

- `resolveLiteralAcceptanceDetailed` — resolve and safety-check, no execute.
- `evaluateScopeCompleteAcceptanceWalk` — already the complete bank-aware path (`reuseMode: "bank"`).
- `readStoredLiteralAcceptanceCommands` / `hasStructuredAcceptanceCommands` — `swarm.verify_commands` is already structured AC.
- `resolveAcReuse` + `hashProductState` + `maybeBankOnAcPass` — durable bank; digest is product plus `plan.acceptance` only.
- `persistVerifyAcSessionCache` / `CachedVerifyAcSnapshot` — already stores commands and runs; complete is profiled off it.
- `skipAcceptanceEvidenceGate` — test-only, not a product skip.

No new resolver. No third complete walker. Extend mint, match, and serve of the existing bank to the resolved ledger.

## Road-not-taken

Rejected: add a bank flag to `evaluateLiteralAcceptanceFromPlan` (two executors remain; the pre-walk still races). Rejected: copy `swarm.verify_commands` onto `plan.acceptance.commands` at mint (makes `commandCount>0` and would enter today's hash, but mutates stated versus derived, leaves the pre-walk executor, and still serves `runs: []`). Rejected: flip complete to `reuseMode: "auto"` so it reads the session cache (the cache already has runs, but it is session-scoped; post-merge complete is often a new session). Rejected: delete only the pre-walk call (the filing already refuses that).

Chosen: keep `evaluateScopeCompleteAcceptanceWalk` as the one complete path, reorder resolve-then-match, persist a cache-shaped snapshot on the bank, keep truly-empty refused.

## Steelman

The strongest reading of the target is that "including a bank minted from executable swarm.verify_commands" already means bind and serve the resolved ledger, and "retain the green-run fact" already means persist runs at mint. Under that reading, finding 1 is specification of matching rather than a hole. What would flip the block to a sharpen: a later map that names `resolveLiteralAcceptanceDetailed` as the pre-reuse step, names that `hashProductState` / `AcPassBankRecord` currently omit the swarm ledger as in-scope work on this issue, and refuses "any bank is a green run" as the #3993 shortcut. Until that map exists, the cheapest reading of the recorded target is delete the first call and the empty-length guard, which is not the whole remedy.

## In plain English

Both cited defects are real: complete still executes before it looks at a bank, and later reuse refuses an empty plan.acceptance.commands even when swarm.verify_commands minted the bank. One bank-aware complete path is the right chokepoint. It is not the whole remedy if matching and serve still key off plan.acceptance.commands and serve runs as empty. Confirming this map restates the remedy as: resolve the literal plus swarm plus narrative contract without executing, persist that ledger and its green-run fact on the durable bank, match against that contract, then execute each resolved command once on a miss. Truly empty stays refused. Swarm-only is eligible only when the resolved executable ledger is non-empty and equals the mint-time ledger. Confirming does not land code and does not ingest this issue.

Forward verdict: restated one-path complete, not delete-the-first-call.

Disposition: accept all four classified headings into contract.

Non-self-arbitration: I authored the Stop 1 write-back. I originated none of the classified findings.

What this arc does not do: it does not implement, it does not ingest, it does not reopen #3993 as a duplicate, it does not weaken clause-walk to treat any bank as a green run.

## Bound remedy (reading of the takes)

1. Keep `evaluateScopeCompleteAcceptanceWalk` as the one complete path. Remove the pre-walk standalone executor. Do not add a second executor or a third walker.
2. Resolve and safety-check via existing `resolveLiteralAcceptanceDetailed` with no execute, then match, then execute each resolved command once on miss.
3. Eligibility matching and bank-serve reconstruction use the resolved literal+swarm+narrative contract, persisted at mint. `plan.acceptance.commands.length` is not that contract. `hashProductState` / `AcPassBankRecord` currently omit the swarm ledger; that omission is in-scope work on this issue.
4. Swarm-only is eligible only when the resolved executable ledger is non-empty and equals the mint-time ledger. Truly empty stays refused. 0-run verified-pass banks are not the swarm-only allow-list.
5. Persist a cache-shaped mint snapshot (commands and runs) onto the durable bank. Do not weaken `clauseWalkBlocks` to "servedFrom=bank implies green run". #3993 is a non-regression on this change.

This lean does not auto-stamp by itself. Operator yolo on the dispatch turn, with "just on github", is recorded as confirm of this all-accept map and as a refuse of ingest/implement from this arc.

With a matching green bank, the regression records zero new command invocations and completes successfully.
Without a bank, every resolved command runs exactly once, never twice.
A bank created from executable `swarm.verify_commands` is eligible even when `plan.acceptance.commands=[]`.
A changed command ledger or newly captured narrative command invalidates or refuses reuse and causes at most one execution.
A stale product-state hash remains fail-closed.
Bank-served results retain the green-run fact needed by clause-walk composition as a #3993 non-regression.
Tests cover both the direct acceptance-walk evaluator and full production transition ordering.
A lifecycle-only completion with a valid matching bank does not invoke the consumer's generic local product build/test wrapper.
No production skip flag, command deletion, or gate weakening is introduced.
